What we can prove, and what we are estimating

The headline materials

How these numbers were built

1 · Start from what we sold

Every confirmed order line for the two years to 31 July 2026. Freight, labour and testing are stripped out.

2 · Run it through the recipe

The live bill of materials for the exact product sold, expanded recursively through our own intermediates until only bought-in raws remain. Archived recipes are a flagged last resort, never the default.

3 · One line per material

Every material name is resolved through a curated identity table, so a material that has carried three codes and four names appears exactly once. A build that meets an unrecognised name fails rather than guessing.

Read this before quoting a number

This is consumption driven by sales, not purchases. It excludes stock movement, wastage, samples and internal use, and it does not spread the custom prescription blends across materials — those are listed separately with a bounded estimate, so nothing here is inflated by guesswork. For blend-heavy materials the factory's actual consumption rate (Coverage & method) is the truer volume.

Liquids are reported in litres and solids in kilograms. They are never added together. Water and packaging are tracked but kept out of the headline.

Year 1 vs year 2 — comparability-gated

Which volumes moved, where the two years are honestly comparable.

The product catalogue was rebuilt mid-window, so many materials switched recipe source between years. A trend is shown ONLY where both years attribute the same way; everything else is listed with its reason rather than pretending to be growth or decline.

Comparable materials, year on year

Not comparable — and why

Coverage & method

How far the numbers can be pushed.

What each confidence tier means, what is deliberately not attributed, everything excluded with its reason, and the checks the model must pass before it is published.

Confidence tiers

Not attributed to a recipe

Real sales with no reliable recipe behind them — mostly one-off prescription blends mixed to a customer's specification. Listed here rather than spread across the materials. Entering recipes for the largest of these lifts coverage most.

Bounded blend estimate

Our own intermediates with no recipe anywhere

Part-made products whose recipe exists in neither the ERP, the master workbook, nor any manufacturing order — their constituent raws are missing from every total. Each is a question for production, not a guess.

Excluded, with reasons

Adjustments and checks

Known soft spots

Blend-heavy materials are understated. The unattributed prescription blends consume urea and calcium nitrate that never reaches these totals — factory consumption since July runs well ahead of the modelled rate for both. Where a negotiation depends on one of these, use the consumption-rate figure, stated as such.

Archived bills of material in the ERP are unreliable — several record tonnes where they mean kilograms. This build only reaches for an archived recipe when every live route fails, and flags every such product.
